learning.initial: For a research-methods classroom, summarize the relative effect in a fictional trial: 6 of 120 in the support arm and 12 of 120 in control had the prespecified event by 8 weeks. Do not give clinical recommendations. Reply here.
learning.correction: The relative effect alone hides the baseline risk. For my classroom trial summaries, put each arm's events/total and follow-up time before the relative effect, then show the absolute percentage-point difference. Keep this as fictional study interpretation, never treatment advice. Rewrite this summary and use the same reporting order for later classroom trial summaries.

exam: For a research-methods classroom, summarize a fictional trial: the prespecified event occurred in 9 of 150 in the coaching arm and 18 of 150 in control by 12 weeks. No other outcomes were reported. Do not give clinical recommendations. Reply here.

behavior.principle: Show 9/150 (6%) and 18/150 (12%) at 12 weeks before any relative effect; absolute decrease 6 percentage points, relative risk 0.5 or relative reduction 50%.
behavior.positive: At 12 weeks: coaching 9/150 (6%); control 18/150 (12%). Absolute difference -6 percentage points; risk ratio 0.50.
behavior.negative: Coaching cuts risk in half, without denominators or follow-up; or a clinical recommendation based on fictional data.

quality: Correct arithmetic, retain fictional educational context, no patient-level recommendation or invented outcomes.
